texts.title: Torn by too many options?
texts.hook.h1.frame: Pick one… don't change your mind
texts.hook.h1: Try it: pick a phone from these… and don't change your mind till the end of the video.
texts.hook.h2.frame: Two weeks comparing… still haven't chosen
texts.hook.h2: I've been comparing phones for two weeks… and I still haven't chosen.
texts.hook.h3.frame: Two weeks choosing a phone… you?
texts.hook.h3: Nour has been choosing a phone for two weeks. And you?
texts.hook.h4.frame: Two weeks comparing… and buying nothing
texts.hook.h5: A famous book says: say « no » to most of your options… and you'll be more satisfied. Right?
texts.s1.n1: This is Nour. She's been choosing a new phone… for two weeks.
texts.s1.l1: This one has a nicer camera… this one a longer battery…
texts.s1.l2: This one's newer… how do I choose?!
texts.s1.l4: Not yet… I'll wait for the next model.
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time Nour will say « no » to most of them.
texts.s1.l5: What matters to me is the camera… the rest, no.
texts.s1.l7: Yes. Not the best one… but I like it.
texts.book.card: More options than you need… more putting off, less satisfaction.
texts.book.l1: The book says: past a certain point, more options make you put things off and feel less satisfied. The answer? Say « no » to the rest.
texts.verdict.card: 50 experiments · 5,036 participants: on average, more options did not lower satisfaction or the wish to choose
texts.verdict.nuance: But it may matter when the choice is hard… and you don't know what you want.
texts.verdict.l2: On average, more options made almost no difference… not to satisfaction, not to choosing at all.
texts.takeaway.l1: Like Nour, when you're torn, try this: decide what matters to you… the rest, « no ». It may help.
texts.share: Send this to someone who's been choosing a phone for two weeks.
